sources.entry: MiroTalk P2P - Simple, secure, fast real-time video conferences up to 4k and 60fps, compatible with all browsers and platforms. (Demo, Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Nodejs/Docker

summary.one_liner: MiroTalk P2P is a self-hosted, open-source WebRTC video conferencing app that uses direct peer-to-peer connections between participants.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a self-hosted video conferencing platform that connects participants directly peer-to-peer over WebRTC, with no central media server in the described architecture. It is deployed by cloning the repo, copying .env and config templates, and running npm start or Docker Compose. Listed features include screen sharing, recording, picture-in-picture, a chat with Markdown and optional GIF search, a collaborative whiteboard, a shared P2P editor, live polls, breakout rooms, and file sharing. It also mentions camera background effects (off, blur, or image) processed in the browser, OIDC auth, room passwords, a REST API, Slack and Mattermost integration, an embeddable iframe and widget, and 133 languages. Claims of 8K at 60fps are stated in the README, and an optional ChatGPT (OpenAI) integration is mentioned.
use_cases: self-hosted video meetings for a team
private video calls without third-party cloud services
embedding video rooms in a website via iframe
running browser-based meetings with screen sharing and whiteboard
hosting webinars or polls in a private room
integrating video calls with Slack or Mattermost
notable: Peer-to-peer WebRTC media, so calls do not route through a central media server, per the README's description
Camera background blur or image replacement processed locally in the browser
Full REST API, webhooks, and Slack/Mattermost integration
Embeddable iframe and widget for other sites
Dual licensing: AGPLv3 free use, with commercial licenses sold on CodeCanyon
caveats: Camera background effects need WebGL2 and load MediaPipe WASM and a model from jsDelivr and Google Storage, which must be reachable under any custom CSP
Background effect output is capped at 1280x720 and 15 FPS, and performance varies by device
Modifications must be released under AGPLv3 unless a commercial license is purchased
